brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Build Your Professional Portfolio with ChatGPT Sites

questions.question: According to the course, what are the four key deliverables you will have by the end of building your professional portfolio?
choices: Portfolio Site, Personal Positioning, Case Study, and AI Assistant
Resume, LinkedIn Profile, Cover Letter, and Portfolio Site
Portfolio Site, Video Introduction, Testimonials, and Certifications
Personal Branding, Social Media Strategy, Business Cards, and Website
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—these four elements work together to create a complete professional presence.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course specifies four specific deliverables that form a complete portfolio system. Review Slide 2 to see all four components and how they work together.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a portfolio and a résumé according to this course?
choices: A portfolio is formatted differently and looks more professional
A résumé lists experience while a portfolio provides proof with context and evidence
A portfolio is longer and includes more detailed job descriptions
A résumé is for employers and a portfolio is only for freelancers
questions.feedback_correct: You've understood the core distinction—a portfolio tells the complete story with proof, not just a list of what you did.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The key difference isn't appearance or length; it's that a portfolio provides evidence and context that answers hiring managers' skepticism, while a résumé leaves questions unanswered.

questions.question: What is the recommended first step before you start building your portfolio website?
choices: Start designing the layout and color scheme
Write a compelling headline that will grab attention
Gather your raw materials like your résumé, headshot, testimonials, and project samples
Create accounts on multiple portfolio hosting platforms
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—gathering your existing materials first sets you up for a faster, more authentic build.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Before you build anything, collect what you already have—your résumé, LinkedIn bio, work samples, certifications, headshot, and testimonials. These become the foundation for your site.

questions.question: According to the course, how much time should you give yourself to build your first portfolio version using ChatGPT Sites?
choices: Several weeks of careful planning and design
Minutes, not days—the goal is speed and momentum with a working version
At least two weeks to ensure quality
One full day dedicated to perfecting every detail
questions.feedback_correct: You've captured the right mindset—done and real beats perfect and delayed.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes speed as a feature, not a bug. A working portfolio you can iterate on is infinitely more valuable than waiting for the perfect version.

questions.question: When you first build your portfolio site, what should you do before making any edits or changes?
choices: Immediately start rewriting sections that feel weak or generic
Ask ChatGPT to completely redesign it for you
Step back and ask five critical review questions to evaluate what's working and what needs improvement
Send it to everyone you know for feedback on the design
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—objective evaluation before editing ensures you focus on what actually matters most.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Resist the urge to immediately edit. Instead, pause and ask five critical questions: What feels strong? What's generic? What's missing? What's too long? What would a visitor understand in 30 seconds?

questions.question: What is the core question that every strong portfolio must answer within the first 30 seconds?
choices: How much experience do you have in your field?
Why should this person be trusted with important work?
What is the most impressive project you have completed?
How much does it cost to hire you for a project?
questions.feedback_correct: You've identified the central purpose of the Portfolio Promise—building trust is what converts visitors into opportunities.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Portfolio Promise is fundamentally about trust. Your value proposition needs to answer this critical question clearly and quickly, before visitors scroll away or make a judgment.

questions.question: Before you apply improvements to your portfolio, the course recommends you first get feedback using a specific prompt—what is the key instruction given in that feedback process?
choices: Have the editor rewrite all weak sections immediately
Identify five generic or unclear elements and prioritize by impact before revising
Focus only on design and layout improvements
Change your entire positioning statement
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—diagnosis before editing prevents wasted effort on low-impact changes.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes 'do not revise yet'—get an honest outside perspective to identify what's holding your portfolio back, then prioritize by impact before making any changes.

questions.question: The course describes a three-pass editing approach for portfolio refinement—what is the goal of Pass 1?
choices: Improve the visual design and layout of your site
Strengthen your case studies with more specific evidence
Clarify the message by ensuring your introduction instantly communicates who you are and who you help
Add more projects and accomplishments to your portfolio
questions.feedback_correct: Right—Pass 1 focuses on the hook, making sure visitors immediately understand your core message.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Pass 1 is about clarifying the message. Your introduction is your hook—make sure it immediately tells visitors who you are and who you help.

questions.question: According to the course, what are the six benchmarks that define a strong first portfolio site?
choices: Beautiful design, mobile-responsive, fast loading, social media integration, video content, and blog posts
Easy to Scan, Specific, Honest, Audience-Aware, Evidence-Based, and Clear Next Steps
Professional photos, multiple case studies, client testimonials, awards, years of experience, and high visibility
Interactive elements, animations, multimedia content, personalized recommendations, AI chatbot, and detailed pricing
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—these six benchmarks focus on clarity and function over complexity, which is exactly what makes portfolios effective.
questions.feedback_incorrect: A strong portfolio doesn't need to be flashy. The six benchmarks are Easy to Scan, Specific, Honest, Audience-Aware, Evidence-Based, and Clear Next Steps—all focused on clarity.

questions.question: The course suggests using ChatGPT as more than just a builder—what specific ongoing role should it play in your professional development after the course ends?
choices: It should replace your need to keep learning new skills
It becomes your Portfolio AI Teammate, capturing new accomplishments, helping create case studies, and keeping your portfolio current as your career evolves
It should automatically post content to your social media accounts
It will send you job opportunities based on your portfolio
questions.feedback_correct: Excellent—you've recognized that the real value is in building a sustainable system, not just a static site.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Portfolio AI Teammate is designed for the long term. It captures accomplishments as they happen, helps you create case studies while they're fresh, and keeps your portfolio current—it's a tool that continues working for you long after the course.
